propositions: RP-01 proposes replacing Rebar's bespoke structured-output orchestration with Pydantic AI seams, but the replacement is not behavior-preserving by default and must reconstruct the behavioral contract from ticket history and test suites before implementation.

Historical bugs encode hard-won behavior around deterministic repair, extraction, refusal/truncation handling, retry limits (three attempts maximum), tool/request budgets, output budgets, provider fallback, usage accounting, telemetry, and failure taxonomy that must be preserved or intentionally changed, not accidentally lost.

Three material Pydantic AI 1.107.2 behaviors require explicit maintainer decision: (1) whether to aggregate all retry attempts into a single operation usage row, (2) how to translate exhaustion errors without blanket-mapping UnexpectedModelBehavior, and (3) whether to add candidate_requests counter for logical fallback/downgrade calls alongside preserved Pydantic requests.

The offline in-process integration probe exercises real Agent, output modes, retry, UsageLimits, FallbackModel, and event-stream seams with mocked transport; it confirmed 19/19 scenarios pass with pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.2 and produced deterministic results for behavioral deltas.

Complete failed responses must be sent on retry only when deterministic fit is proven; otherwise omitted whole—never prefix-truncated—to prevent silent loss of material findings and preserve correct auditing.

Length/max_tokens finish reason must be rejected before parse/repair as an unretryable condition, consuming the bounded output-retry allowance with explicit concise-response guidance; refusal and content-filter remain terminal after one call.
